coverage_explanation: Checks all ten outputs at both ADC endpoints, verifies an interior illuminated prefix and unilluminated suffix without requiring a rounding convention, and checks return to zero after illumination. Exact quantization boundaries are not tested because rounding is unspecified. The requirement also gives no maximum response time: the fixed-time host API cannot express eventual completion without a deadline. Observations therefore use generous four-second settling windows as a finite bench accommodation, not a requirement-derived timing limit; arbitrarily slow implementations remain outside this test's coverage.
assumptions: Uses the explicit circuit, not bench-default wiring: segments 1 through 10 are active HIGH on digital pins 2 through 11, and the potentiometer signal is A0.
Mapping 0–1023 to 0–10 preserves the endpoints and represents a linear bar level. Integer rounding is unspecified; interior checks omit segments whose status could depend on rounding.
The bar consists of an illuminated prefix starting at segment 1, consistent with 'up to the mapped value'. The success criterion does not refer to Arduino digital pin numbers as bar indices.
No polling period or maximum startup/update latency is supplied. Four-second settling is a practical observation allowance only; this test cannot establish unrestricted eventual response.
The reference uses Arduino integer map as one permitted quantization choice, but checks do not require its particular transition thresholds.
Resistor-value inconsistencies do not change the host-level active-HIGH GPIO expectations.
